source.title: Find All Possible Stable Binary Arrays I

teaching.hint: What does a violating all-equal subarray say about a run of equal values?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: The condition is exactly that no equal-value run exceeds `limit`; counting can depend on the used zeros, used ones, and final value.
solution_outline.approach: Count arrays ending in each bit for each pair of used quantities. Extend shorter arrays by one bit, then subtract extensions whose prior final run already had length `limit`; seed the one-value boundaries by their run limit.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Each table entry counts exactly stable arrays with its two counts and final bit; the subtraction removes precisely the newly overlong runs.
solution_outline.correctness: Appending one bit preserves all old windows. The only new violation is a final run of length `limit+1`, which is in bijection with a shorter stable array ending in the opposite bit followed by `limit` copies.
solution_outline.complexity: `O(zero·one)` time and space for the compressed count; a run-length state uses `O(zero·one·limit)` time and space.
solution_outline.pitfall: Missing one-value base cases or mishandling modular subtraction corrupts the recurrence.

common_wrong_turns: Treat the all-subarray condition as unrelated windows
source_fidelity_notes: The quantified subarray condition and exact counts remain explicit; source enumeration example is omitted.
